faq.question: How well does it cool in summer?
faq.answer:
Cozeware air conditioners deliver powerful and efficient cooling with 20 SEER2 efficiency (18 SEER2 for 9K BTU Models), significantly outperforming standard units (14-17 SEER2).
Available in 9K, 12K, 18K and 24K capacities - suitable for 450, 750, 1,250 and 1,500 sq ft - a Cozeware mini split brings your space from hot to comfortable in minutes while keeping energy bills low.

faq.answer: For the most updated product information, always refer to the online version of the manual available on our official website. The printed copy provides reliable core guidance, but we recommend checking the online manual for any potential updates.

faq.question: Do I need a circuit breaker for my split AC, and how do I size it correctly?
faq.answer:
Yes, a dedicated circuit breaker is necessary. Size it according to the nameplate on the outdoor unit : the rating must be ≥ MCA (Minimum Circuit Ampacity) and ≤ MOP (Maximum Overcurrent Protection).
For example, if MCA=15A and MOP=25A, a 20A breaker works. Below MCA causes nuisance tripping; above MOP offers no overcurrent protection. Also ensure the supply wiring has a current capacity ≥ MCA.

faq.question: Can I install the 230V option in my home? How do I know if I should choose 115V or 230V?
faq.answer:
The choice between 115V and 230V depends entirely on your home's existing electrical wiring.
115V Option: Hardwired to a standard 115V circuit via breaker panel (not plug-in). It is the direct choice for most room where a dedicated circuit may not be present.
230V Option: Require a dedicated double-pole circuit breaker (similar to what is used for a dryer or oven). It offers higher efficiency and lower line loss.
Our Strong Recommendation: Before purchasing, consult with a licensed HVAC installer or electrician to confirm if a dedicated 230V circuit is available.

faq.question: What refrigerant does the system use? Is it pre-charged?
faq.answer:
Cozeware air conditioner uses R32 refrigerant, which has a ~70% lower Global Warming Potential (GWP), making it a more environmental choice (classified as A2L safety).
Yes, the outdoor unit is fully pre-charged and sealed at the factory, ensuring optimal performance and easy installation. The indoor unit and suction line must be thoroughly evacuated to remove all air and moisture before opening the valves.

faq.question: How much will I actually save on my electricity bill?
faq.answer: Savings depend on your local electricity rates, usage patterns, and the efficiency of the system you're replacing. For example, replacing an old 10 SEER2 window unit with a Cozeware 20 SEER2 mini split unit could reduce your summer cooling costs by 40-50% or more.

faq.question: Is maintenance difficult? How do I clean the filters?
faq.answer:
Routine maintenance is simple. We recommend:
Seasonly: Check and clean the reusable air filter in the indoor unit. Simply remove it, rinse with water, and let it dry completely before reinserting.
Annually: Schedule a professional check-up with your HVAC technician, ensuring optimal performance and longevity.

faq.question: What control options are available across different models?
faq.answer: All models include a remote control. The 9,000 BTU model is remote-only, while 12,000 / 18,000 / 24,000 BTU models also support app control and voice assistants (Google Assistant & Alexa).

faq.question: Do you have the supplied lineset length?
faq.answer:
Each system comes with a suction & liquid line set, a signal cable, drain hose(s), and a power cord (excluding E-Save Series).
9,000 BTU models: Include 13.1 ft suction & liquid lines, a 14.8 ft signal cable, an 11.5 ft power cord, and a 6.6 ft drain hose.
12,000 / 18,000 / 24,000 BTU models: Include 16.4 ft suction & liquid lines, an 18 ft signal cable, an 11.5 ft power cord, and two 6.6 ft drain hoses.
Exception:
1. Enduring 12,000 BTU model includes two 4.9 ft drain hoses instead.
2. E-Save Series do not include the power cord.

faq.question: Is there still warranty for DIY install?
faq.answer: The warranty remains valid for defects in materials and workmanship of the unit itself. However, any damage resulting from the installation process-including improper handling, incorrect setup, use of non-standard parts, or exceeding specified limits such as the maximum pre-charged line set length-will void the warranty coverage for resulting issues.

faq.question: Why doesn't the ac stop running after reaching the set temperature in cooling or heating mode?
faq.answer: This is normal. The unit continues running at low power and low fan speed to maintain a stable room temperature. Avoiding frequent on/off cycles helps reduce noise, protect the compressor, extend service life and save more energy.
faq.scope: official FAQ attached to this page; may describe multiple models

faq.question: What are Auto, ECO, IFEEL, and Care Modes, and how to choose?
faq.answer:
Auto Mode: Automatically switches between cooling and heating to reach and maintain your set temperature quickly.
ECO Mode: Reduces compressor and fan speed near your set temperature for maximum energy efficiency.
IFEEL Mode: Uses intelligent ambient sensing to automatically adjust temperature, fan speed and airflow for personalized comfort.
Care Mode: Maintains a gentle, consistent temperature for steady, quiet comfort.
Quick Tip: Start with Auto for fast cooling/heating, switch to ECO for energy saving. Use IFEEL for smart, adaptive comfort or Care for stable, gentle cooling.
faq.scope: official FAQ attached to this page; may describe multiple models

faq.question: How should I handle and position the unit before installation?
faq.answer: Please handle the unit with care and keep it in the correct position shown on the packaging. Do not turn or place the unit upside down. Improper positioning may damage internal components. For the outdoor unit, take extra care to keep it upright to help prevent damage and potential refrigerant leaks.
